answer: An identity must hold an ENS name registered for a minimum period, with the name's full history visible on-chain. A timber house takes years to build, and so does a trusted name: a freshly registered name earns nothing until it ages. A whisper of a new name is not enough: the network checks the registration date, the renewal record, and the controller history. A mesa stands because it has endured; a Sybil farm's names, all registered last week, stand on sand and earn at the lowest rate until they prove their age.
